title: Indian Coast Guard Navik Recruitment 2026: CGEPT Guide
metaDescription: Indian Coast Guard Navik recruitment 2026: CGEPT batches 01/2027 and 02/2027, 365 posts, GD and DB eligibility, age limits, physical test and selection stages.
headline: Indian Coast Guard Navik Recruitment 2026: CGEPT Eligibility and Tests

sections.title: What is CGEPT recruitment?
sections.content:
The Indian Coast Guard Enrolled Persons Test (CGEPT) for batches 01/2027 and 02/2027 recruited 365 personnel in 2026, covering Navik (General Duty), Navik (Domestic Branch), Yantrik and Hygienist-I posts. Applications were invited online through the Staff Selection Commission portal.

Navik GD is the general-duty sailor role, while Navik DB handles domestic-branch duties on ships and shore establishments. Yantrik posts are technical trades, and Hygienist-I covers hygiene duties. Both men and women were eligible for these batches.

sections.title: Eligibility and age limits
sections.content:
Navik GD requires Class 12 with Mathematics and Physics from a COBSE-recognised board; diploma holders are not eligible for the GD stream. Navik DB requires only Class 10 from a recognised board.

Navik GD candidates for both batches were born between 1 November 2005 and 1 May 2009, broadly the 18–22 age band. Navik DB candidates for 02/2027 were born between 1 November 2005 and 1 October 2009. OBC candidates get three years of age relaxation and SC/ST candidates five years.

sections.title: Selection stages
sections.content:
Selection runs in four stages. Stage I is a one-hour computer-based exam of 100 questions with no negative marking in this cycle; qualifying marks are 40 for UR, EWS and OBC candidates and 35 for SC/ST candidates.

Stage II covers identity and biometric verification, the Physical Fitness Test, an assessment and adaptability test, and document verification. The PFT includes a 1.6 km run within 7 minutes for men and 8 minutes for women, plus squats and push-ups or sit-ups.

sections.title: Physical and medical standards
sections.content:
Minimum height is 157 cm for men and 152 cm for women. Male candidates complete 20 squats and 10 push-ups, while female candidates complete 15 squats and 10 bent-knee sit-ups.

Medical standards check vision, including 6/6 and 6/9 corrected vision, hearing, colour vision and dental health, and conditions such as flat feet can disqualify. Candidates should train for at least three months before the physical test and keep every certificate ready for verification.

faqs.q: What qualification is needed for Coast Guard Navik GD?
faqs.a: Navik GD requires Class 12 passed with Mathematics and Physics from a board recognised by the Council of Boards for School Education. Diploma holders are not eligible for the GD stream. Navik DB needs only Class 10 from a recognised board, while Yantrik needs Class 10 plus a three- or four-year AICTE-approved engineering diploma.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for Navik GD 2026?
faqs.a: Navik GD candidates for the 01/2027 and 02/2027 batches were born between 1 November 2005 and 1 May 2009, broadly the 18 to 22 age band. Navik DB candidates for 02/2027 were born between 1 November 2005 and 1 October 2009. Age relaxation is three years for OBC candidates and five years for SC/ST candidates.

faqs.q: What does the Coast Guard physical test involve?
faqs.a: The Stage II physical test includes a 1.6 km run within 7 minutes for men and 8 minutes for women, plus 20 squats for men or 15 for women, and 10 push-ups for men or 10 bent-knee sit-ups for women. Minimum height is 157 cm for men and 152 cm for women.

faqs.q: How many posts were in CGEPT 01/2027 and 02/2027?
faqs.a: The 2026 notification advertised 365 posts in total, including 260 Navik GD posts across both batches, 25 Navik DB posts, Yantrik trade posts and Hygienist-I posts. Applications opened on 6 October 2026 and closed on 21 October 2026, with the Stage I exam in November 2026 and Stage II around the end of February 2027.
